title: Nyāyatattva
summary: Nāthamuni's lost work on logic and the means of knowledge, which later Viśiṣṭādvaita logicians (Vedānta Deśika's Nyāyapariśuddhi) say they follow; known only from citations.

tradition.text: Nāthamuni, traditionally 9th–10th c. (hagiographies give an extremely long life)

title: Yogarahasya (of Nāthamuni)
summary: Nāthamuni's lost treatise on (aṣṭāṅga) yoga, which the hagiographies say he taught to Kurukai Kāvalappaṉ; the original is lost. A text published in the 20th century under this title is claimed in T. Krishnamacharya's lineage as a recovery; that claim belongs to lin:krishnamacharya and is not accepted here as the original.

tradition.text: Nāthamuni, traditionally 9th–10th c. (hagiographies give an extremely long life)

title: Puruṣanirṇaya
summary: A lost work attributed to Nāthamuni, said to establish the identity of the supreme Person (Nārāyaṇa); known only by name.

tradition.text: Nāthamuni, traditionally 9th–10th c. (hagiographies give an extremely long life)

title: Siddhitraya
summary: Yāmuna's three 'proofs': Ātmasiddhi (the self is distinct from body, senses, mind and cognition and is known as the 'I'), Īśvarasiddhi (on establishing the Lord) and Saṃvitsiddhi (against Advaita's objectless consciousness); the Īśvarasiddhi and Saṃvitsiddhi survive only partly.

tradition.text: Yāmuna, 916–1041 CE in one traditional reckoning

title: Stotraratna
summary: Yāmuna's hymn to Nārāyaṇa (c. 65 verses) opening with homage to Nāthamuni, Parāśara and Nammāḻvār, praising the Lord's supremacy and qualities, and culminating in the poet's confession of helplessness (ākiñcanya) and surrender at the Lord's feet.

tradition.text: Yāmuna, 916–1041 CE in one traditional reckoning

title: Catuḥślokī
summary: Yāmuna's four verses in praise of Śrī (Lakṣmī), declaring that even the Lord cannot measure her greatness and that she is the Lord's consort, whose servants are all the gods; later the Vaṭakalai cite it for Śrī's supremacy.

tradition.text: Yāmuna, 916–1041 CE in one traditional reckoning

title: Mahāpuruṣanirṇaya
summary: A work attributed to Yāmuna establishing Nārāyaṇa as the supreme Person; regarded as lost.

tradition.text: Yāmuna, 916–1041 CE in one traditional reckoning

title: Śrībhāṣya
summary: Rāmānuja's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras following, he says, Bodhāyana's lost Vṛtti. Its first sūtra contains the 'great prior view' (mahāpūrvapakṣa) of Advaita and its refutation (mahāsiddhānta), including the seven untenables of avidyā; the whole establishes Brahman as the qualified cause of the world, the soul as its mode, bhakti-meditation as the means and liberation as reaching Brahman by the path of light.

structure.description: 4 adhyāyas × 4 pādas, following the sūtras (Rāmānuja's sūtra division differs slightly from Śaṅkara's)

title: Vedārthasaṅgraha
summary: Rāmānuja's independent treatise on the meaning of the Upaniṣads: it criticizes the views of Śaṅkara, Bhāskara and Yādavaprakāśa, classifies scriptural texts into those of difference, non-difference and mediation (ghaṭaka), reads 'tat tvam asi' by co-reference, and establishes Nārāyaṇa as the supreme Brahman reached through bhakti.

title: Vedāntasāra (of Rāmānuja)
summary: A brief commentary by Rāmānuja on the Brahma Sūtras (distinct from Sadānanda's Advaita Vedāntasāra, src:vedantasara).

title: Vedāntadīpa
summary: Rāmānuja's middle-length commentary on the Brahma Sūtras, clarifying the Śrībhāṣya's reading of each sūtra.

title: Gītābhāṣya of Rāmānuja
summary: Rāmānuja's commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā: the Lord of Śrī descended as Kṛṣṇa teaches bhakti-yoga, prepared by karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga; the plurality of selves is real; verse 18.66 is read both as renunciation of agency in the yogas and as surrender for those unable to begin bhakti.

title: Gadyatraya
summary: Rāmānuja's three prose hymns: the Śaraṇāgati Gadya (surrender to Śrī and then to Nārāyaṇa, with the Lord's answer), the Śrīraṅga Gadya (surrender to Raṅganātha) and the Śrīvaikuṇṭha Gadya (meditation on the Lord in Vaikuṇṭha).

attribution.scholarly: authenticity questioned by some modern scholars (e.g. R. C. Lester), defended by others

title: Śaraṇāgati Gadya
summary: Rāmānuja's prose act of surrender, set on the day of Paṅguni Uttiram at Śrīraṅgam: he takes refuge in Śrī, then in Nārāyaṇa, asks for supreme devotion, knowledge and love (parabhakti, parajñāna, paramabhakti), and records the Lord's reply granting all and bidding him dwell at Śrīraṅgam reciting the dvaya.

attribution.scholarly: authenticity questioned by some modern scholars (e.g. R. C. Lester), defended by others

title: Śrīraṅga Gadya
summary: A short prose surrender to Raṅganātha at Śrīraṅgam, asking to become his eternal servant.

attribution.scholarly: authenticity questioned by some modern scholars (e.g. R. C. Lester), defended by others

title: Śrīvaikuṇṭha Gadya
summary: A prose meditation on Vaikuṇṭha, the Lord seated there with Śrī, Bhū and Nīlā amid the eternal servants, prescribed for one who has surrendered.

attribution.scholarly: authenticity questioned by some modern scholars (e.g. R. C. Lester), defended by others

title: Nityagrantha
summary: A short manual attributed to Rāmānuja on the daily worship (ārādhana) of the Lord at home by the Śrīvaiṣṇava, following Pāñcarātra procedure.

attribution.scholarly: authenticity questioned by some modern scholars (e.g. R. C. Lester), defended by others

title: Pañcastava
summary: Kūreśa's five hymns — Śrīvaikuṇṭhastava, Atimānuṣastava, Sundarabāhustava, Varadarājastava and Śrīstava — praising the Lord's transcendence, his descents, the deities of Tirumāliruñcōlai and Kāñcī, and Śrī.

title: Śrīraṅgarājastava
summary: Parāśara Bhaṭṭar's hymn in two centuries (pūrva and uttara śataka) to Raṅganātha of Śrīraṅgam, describing the temple and the Lord's qualities and ending in surrender.

title: Śrīguṇaratnakośa
summary: Parāśara Bhaṭṭar's hymn to Śrī (Raṅganāyakī), praising her qualities and her motherly mediation.

title: Aṣṭaślokī
summary: Eight verses by Parāśara Bhaṭṭar explaining the three secret mantras (tirumantra, dvaya, carama-śloka).

title: Irāmāṉuca Nūṟṟantāti
summary: Tiruvaraṅgattu Amudaṉār's 108 Tamil verses in antāti form praising Rāmānuja as the refuge of the surrendered; included in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham and called the 'Prapanna Gāyatrī'.

title: Jñānasāram
summary: Forty Tamil verses by Aruḷāḷa Perumāḷ Emperumāṉār (the former Advaitin Yajñamūrti) on the essentials of surrender and devotion to the teacher.

title: Prameyasāram
summary: Ten Tamil verses by Aruḷāḷa Perumāḷ Emperumāṉār summarizing the meaning of the tirumantra and the glory of the teacher.

title: Ārāyirappaṭi (the 'Six Thousand')
summary: The first commentary on Nammāḻvār's Tiruvāymoḻi, in Maṇipravāḷa of about 6,000 granthas, written by Tirukkurukaippirāṉ Piḷḷāṉ at Rāmānuja's direction, reading the hymns in the light of Viśiṣṭādvaita.

title: Oṉpatiṉāyirappaṭi (the 'Nine Thousand')
summary: Nañjīyar's Maṇipravāḷa commentary on the Tiruvāymoḻi; the tradition says the copy made by Nampiḷḷai was lost in the Kāvēri and rewritten by him from memory.

title: Irupattunālāyirappaṭi (the 'Twenty-four Thousand')
summary: Periyavāccāṉ Piḷḷai's Maṇipravāḷa commentary on the Tiruvāymoḻi, modelled on the length of the Rāmāyaṇa.

title: Īṭu Muppattāṟāyirappaṭi (the 'Thirty-six Thousand')
summary: The fullest commentary on the Tiruvāymoḻi: Nampiḷḷai's lectures as written down by Vaṭakku Tiruvīti Piḷḷai, transmitted orally through the teachers to Maṇavāḷa Māmuni, who expounded it before Raṅganātha for a year.

title: Paṉṉīrāyirappaṭi (the 'Twelve Thousand')
summary: A commentary on the Tiruvāymoḻi by Vādikesari Aḻagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar, giving word-by-word meanings.

title: Guruparamparāprabhāvam (Ārāyirappaṭi)
summary: The Maṇipravāḷa hagiography of the Āḻvārs and ācāryas attributed to Piṉpaḻagiya Perumāḷ Jīyar: the source of the stories of Nāthamuni's recovery of the Prabandham, Yāmuna's three folded fingers, Rāmānuja's teachers and the six sayings of Varadarāja.

title: Guruparamparāprabhāvam (Mūvāyirappaṭi)
summary: The Vaṭakalai hagiography of the teacher lineage, the 'Three Thousand', traditionally attributed to the third Brahmatantra Svatantra Jīyar.
notes: Attribution recalled with low confidence: the tradition names 'the third' holder of the Brahmatantra Svatantra title, not necessarily Deśika's own disciple.

title: Divyasūricaritam
summary: A Sanskrit poem on the lives of the Āḻvārs and of Rāmānuja, attributed to Garuḍavāhana Paṇḍita, whom the tradition makes a contemporary of Rāmānuja.

title: Prapannāmṛtam
summary: A Sanskrit hagiography of the Śrīvaiṣṇava teachers by Anantārya (Anantācārya).

title: Yatīndrapravaṇa Prabhāvam
summary: The Teṅkalai hagiography of Maṇavāḷa Māmuni by Piḷḷai Lokam Jīyar, recording his life, his year-long exposition of the Īṭu before Raṅganātha and the Lord's gift of the taniyaṉ 'śrīśaileśa-dayāpātram'.

title: Śrutaprakāśikā
summary: Sudarśana Sūri's great sub-commentary on the Śrībhāṣya, recording, the tradition says, the lectures of Naḍādūr Ammāḷ; the standard gloss of the Śrībhāṣya for both later schools. The tradition says Vedānta Deśika saved its manuscript during the sack of Śrīraṅgam.

title: Rahasyatrayasāra
summary: Deśika's Maṇipravāḷa summa of the Śrīvaiṣṇava way of surrender, in 32 chapters (adhikāras): the five things to be known, the three realities, the supreme deity, the qualified, prapatti with its limbs as an independent means, conduct after surrender, offences and their removal, departure and the path of light, the three secret mantras, and the duties of teacher and disciple.

title: Tattvamuktākalāpa
summary: Deśika's systematic poem of about 500 verses in five sections (sara): insentient substance, the soul, the Lord (nāyaka), cognition (buddhi) and non-substances (adravya), refuting rival schools; with his own commentary Sarvārthasiddhi.

title: Sarvārthasiddhi (on the Tattvamuktākalāpa)
summary: Deśika's own prose commentary on his Tattvamuktākalāpa (distinct from Pūjyapāda's Jain Sarvārthasiddhi).

title: Śatadūṣaṇī
summary: Deśika's polemic against Advaita, planned as a hundred refutations (vāda) of which about sixty-six survive, attacking the attributeless Brahman, the unreality of the world, avidyā and liberation while living.

title: Nyāyasiddhāñjana
summary: Deśika's treatise on the categories of Viśiṣṭādvaita — insentient substance, soul, Lord, the eternal realm, cognition and non-substances.

title: Nyāyapariśuddhi
summary: Deśika's 'purification of Nyāya': Viśiṣṭādvaita logic and epistemology (perception, inference, scripture, and the theory of error), following Nāthamuni's lost Nyāyatattva and correcting Nyāya where it conflicts with Vedānta.

title: Tattvaṭīkā
summary: Deśika's (incomplete) sub-commentary on the Śrībhāṣya.

title: Adhikaraṇasārāvalī
summary: Deśika's verse summary of each topic (adhikaraṇa) of the Brahma Sūtras as read in the Śrībhāṣya.

title: Mīmāṃsāpādukā
summary: Deśika's verse work on Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, read theistically as one science with Vedānta.

title: Seśvaramīmāṃsā
summary: Deśika's commentary on the Mīmāṃsā Sūtras arguing that Pūrva Mīmāṃsā, rightly read, presupposes the Lord and forms one science (aikaśāstrya) with the Brahma Sūtras.

title: Tātparyacandrikā (of Vedānta Deśika)
summary: Deśika's sub-commentary on Rāmānuja's Gītābhāṣya. (Id disambiguated from Vyāsatīrtha's Dvaita Tātparyacandrikā, which U15 records as src:tatparyacandrika; U05 used src:tatparyacandrika for this work — merge must separate them.)

title: Rahasyarakṣā
summary: Deśika's commentary on Yāmuna's Stotraratna and Catuḥślokī and on Rāmānuja's Gadyas, defending Śrī's supremacy and the doctrine of surrender.

title: Nikṣeparakṣā
summary: Deśika's Sanskrit defence of prapatti (nikṣepa, self-deposit) as a scriptural, independent means to liberation, against objections.

title: Saccaritrarakṣā
summary: Deśika's treatise defending Śrīvaiṣṇava conduct: the marks of discus and conch, the vertical forehead mark and the taking of the Lord's remnants.

title: Pādukāsahasra
summary: Deśika's 1,008 verses in 32 sections (paddhati) on the sandals of Raṅganātha, composed, the tradition says, in a single night; the sandals are Nammāḻvār (Śaṭhakopa) and the teacher who carries the Lord to the devotee.

title: Dayāśataka
summary: Deśika's hundred and more verses to the Compassion (Dayā) of Śrīnivāsa of Tirumala, personified as a goddess.

title: Nyāsadaśaka
summary: Ten verses by Deśika on self-surrender (nyāsa), including the offering that the self, its protection and the fruit of protection belong not to oneself but to Śrī's Lord.

title: Nyāsaviṃśati
summary: Twenty verses by Deśika summarizing the doctrine of surrender: the qualified, the teacher, the limbs and the result.

title: Nyāsatilaka
summary: Deśika's hymn to Raṅganātha on surrender.

title: Saṅkalpasūryodaya
summary: Deśika's allegorical drama in ten acts on the soul's liberation (King Viveka against Mahāmoha), written as a Viśiṣṭādvaita answer to Kṛṣṇamiśra's Prabodhacandrodaya.

title: Yādavābhyudaya
summary: Deśika's great poem (mahākāvya) on the life of Kṛṣṇa; the tradition says Appayya Dīkṣita wrote a commentary on it.

title: Haṃsasandeśa
summary: Deśika's messenger poem in which Rāma sends a swan to Sītā in Laṅkā.

title: Abhītistava
summary: Deśika's hymn to Raṅganātha for freedom from fear, composed, the tradition says, during the troubles at Śrīraṅgam.

title: Hayagrīvastotra
summary: Deśika's hymn to Hayagrīva, the horse-headed form of the Lord as the giver of knowledge.

title: Varadarājapañcāśat
summary: Deśika's fifty verses to Varadarāja of Kāñcī.

title: Śrīstuti
summary: Deśika's hymn to Śrī (Lakṣmī), praising her as the Lord's inseparable consort and co-refuge.

title: Godāstuti
summary: Deśika's hymn to Godā (Āṇṭāḷ).

title: Vairāgyapañcaka
summary: Five verses by Deśika declining royal patronage — the tradition says in reply to an invitation conveyed by Vidyāraṇya to the Vijayanagara court — declaring the Lord his only wealth.

title: Lokācāryapañcāśat
summary: Fifty verses in praise of Piḷḷai Lokācārya that the Teṅkalai tradition attributes to Vedānta Deśika; the attribution is not accepted by all.

title: Dramiḍopaniṣat-tātparya-ratnāvalī
summary: Deśika's Sanskrit verses giving the purport of each decad of Nammāḻvār's Tiruvāymoḻi (the 'Tamil Upaniṣad'), in terms of the Lord's qualities.

title: Dramiḍopaniṣat-sāra
summary: Deśika's short Sanskrit summary of the teaching of the Tiruvāymoḻi.

title: Aḍaikkalappattu
summary: Deśika's ten Tamil verses of surrender (aḍaikkalam, 'refuge') to Varadarāja of Kāñcī.

title: Paramapadasopānam
summary: Deśika's Tamil–Maṇipravāḷa work on the 'steps to the supreme abode': nine steps from discrimination (viveka) through disgust with the world, dispassion, fear, gaining the Lord's favour (by surrender), departure from the body, the path of light and arrival in the divine realm to attainment.

title: Deśika Prabandham
summary: The collection of Vedānta Deśika's Tamil poems (Aḍaikkalappattu, Mummaṇikkōvai, Navamaṇimālai and others).

title: Adhikaraṇacintāmaṇi
summary: Commentary by Kumāra Varadācārya, Deśika's son, on his father's Adhikaraṇasārāvalī.

title: Mumukṣuppaṭi
summary: Piḷḷai Lokācārya's aphoristic Maṇipravāḷa work for 'one seeking liberation' on the three secret mantras — the tirumantra, the dvaya and the carama-śloka — in three sections.

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Śrīvacanabhūṣaṇam
summary: Piḷḷai Lokācārya's chief work, in aphorisms: the glory of Śrī's mediation, the Lord as the sole means, the conduct of the surrendered, service to devotees, and finally the saving power of the teacher's regard (ācārya-abhimāna).

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Tattvatrayam
summary: Piḷḷai Lokācārya's aphoristic exposition of the three realities: cit (souls), acit (matter in three kinds) and Īśvara.

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Arthapañcakam
summary: Piḷḷai Lokācārya's short work on the five things a seeker must know — the self, the Lord, the means, the goal and the obstacle — each in five kinds.

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Arcirādi
summary: Piḷḷai Lokācārya's short work on the path of light (arcirādi-gati) by which the liberated soul travels to Vaikuṇṭha.

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Navavidhasambandham
summary: A short work in Piḷḷai Lokācārya's collection on the nine relations between the Lord and the soul contained in the tirumantra.

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Prameyaśekharam
summary: One of Piḷḷai Lokācārya's eighteen 'secret' works (rahasya).

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Aṣṭādaśa Rahasyaṅgaḷ (the eighteen rahasyas)
summary: The collection of Piḷḷai Lokācārya's eighteen short Maṇipravāḷa works on the secret doctrine, including the Mumukṣuppaṭi, Tattvatrayam, Śrīvacanabhūṣaṇam, Arthapañcakam and Arcirādi.

tradition.text: Piḷḷai Lokācārya, 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates

title: Ācārya Hṛdayam
summary: Aphorisms by Aḻagiya Maṇavāḷa Perumāḷ Nāyaṉār, younger brother of Piḷḷai Lokācārya, setting out the 'heart' of Nammāḻvār: the Tiruvāymoḻi as the Tamil Veda equal to the Sanskrit, and the Āḻvār's teaching of surrender.

title: Śrīvacanabhūṣaṇa-vyākhyānam
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's commentary on the Śrīvacanabhūṣaṇam, the standard Teṅkalai reading of the work.

title: Mumukṣuppaṭi-vyākhyānam
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's commentary on the Mumukṣuppaṭi.

title: Tattvatraya-vyākhyānam
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's commentary on Piḷḷai Lokācārya's Tattvatrayam.

title: Ācāryahṛdaya-vyākhyānam
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's commentary on the Ācārya Hṛdayam.

title: Upadēśa Ratnamālai
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's Tamil verses recounting the Āḻvārs' birth-stars, the commentaries on the Prabandham and the teacher lineage down to Piḷḷai Lokācārya, urging devotion to the Śrīvacanabhūṣaṇam.

title: Tiruvāymoḻi Nūṟṟantāti
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's hundred Tamil verses summarizing each decad of the Tiruvāymoḻi.

title: Yatirājaviṃśati
summary: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni's twenty Sanskrit verses to Rāmānuja (Yatirāja), confessing faults and seeking refuge in him.

title: Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam
summary: The dawn hymn to Veṅkaṭeśvara of Tirumala (with its Stotra, Prapatti and Maṅgaḷāśāsana), attributed to Prativādi Bhayaṅkaram Aṇṇaṉ, a disciple of Maṇavāḷa Māmuni.

title: Tattvasāra (of Vātsya Varadaguru)
summary: Verses by Vātsya Varadaguru (Naḍādūr Ammāḷ) on the chief doctrinal points of the Śrībhāṣya.

title: Nyāyakuliśa
summary: A treatise on Viśiṣṭādvaita logic by Ātreya Rāmānuja (Kiḍāmbi Appuḷḷār), Deśika's uncle and teacher.

title: Nayadyumaṇi
summary: A treatise on the means of knowledge and categories by Meghanādāri Sūri, a Viśiṣṭādvaita logician before Deśika.

title: Caṇḍamāruta
summary: Doḍḍayācārya's commentary on Deśika's Śatadūṣaṇī, continuing the polemic against Advaita.

title: Upaniṣat-prakāśikā
summary: Raṅgarāmānuja Muni's commentaries on the principal Upaniṣads from the Viśiṣṭādvaita standpoint.

title: Yatīndramatadīpikā
summary: Śrīnivāsadāsa's primer of Viśiṣṭādvaita in ten chapters (avatāra): perception, inference and scripture as the means of knowledge; then the realities — prakṛti, time, the eternal realm, attributive consciousness, the soul, the Lord — and the non-substances.
